note: THE BYTES COLUMN of 201/1-01, and the last table the step owed. Same phone, same pak (`build/phone-ls-rgba8/pak`, 02:47 09-08-2026, rgba8, --max-texture 256) and same pinned district as the 08-09 frame row, taken with the camera WORKED — down to street level (h 25.7) and across the district — because the column fills with what the streamer requests and a static camera asks for almost nothing after the first load. 799 frames / 33.1 s, `warnings` empty. It is a second capture, not a replacement: its frame numbers describe a harder camera at a lower eye than the 08-09 baseline row and are recorded here for context rather than as a revision of it. ARTEFACT GONE (noted 2026-08-09): see the texture-budget row of the same day — `build/phone-ls-rgba8` was a symlink sharing one directory with three other pak names, and later ASTC converts overwrote the pak this capture ran against. The capture itself is unaffected: it was taken live, and every number in it came out of the running console.

runs.surface: dispatch console, ?inventory=1&district=los-santos-centre, camera worked to street level

againstWhatTheBuildContains.textureArrays: 31 104 178 B read over 20 requests, against a deflated texture payload of 31 142 707 B in the pak — 99.9 %, and 20 arrays of 20. On this district the surface reads EVERY texture the build carries. There is no unread texture to omit; the lever is the format (ASTC would make the same content 23.4 MB resident instead of 99.7) and the cap, not selection.
againstWhatTheBuildContains.cellEntries: The pak holds 8 cell entries for its 4 cells (hd + lod). The run read 4 hd and 3 lod — one LOD entry was never requested, which is the ring policy behaving: a cell whose HD stays resident at this eye never needs its LOD.
againstWhatTheBuildContains.collision: ZERO requests. The pak carries a baked collision bake — 9 cells on the game grid, 565 regions, 49 870 triangles, 100 breakable — and the dispatch surface asked for none of it, in 33 seconds of working the camera. Confirmed in code as well as in the capture: `bootDispatch` never touches `setup.collision`, because the map runs no physics. This is the first hard evidence for 1/03's conditional candidate, and it is the only thing the build contains that this surface provably never reads.
againstWhatTheBuildContains.water: 2 658 756 B in one request — 7.3 % of everything read, for a mesh whose whole job is to say 'this is the ocean, not missing data'. Not a candidate for removal (a map without a shoreline reads as a hole), but the largest single non-texture read and a candidate for a cheaper representation.

readings.whatAMapACTUALLYreads: 85.4 % of the bytes are texture arrays, 7.3 % water, 7.3 % cell geometry. A profile that hunts for unread entry KINDS finds exactly one — collision — and everything else is read in full.
readings.theFrameIsStillWAITING: 15.9 % of the frame inside the loop this time, against 21.2 % on the baseline row: a lower eye and a moving camera made the frame longer without making the main thread busier. The direction is the same and stronger — the cost is downstream of the CPU.
readings.overlay2dGrewWithTheWork: 3.05 ms against 2.44 on the baseline, still the largest item in the body and still drawing nine units. Whatever it scales with, it is not unit count alone.
readings.aONEsecondBodyStall: `cpuBodyMaxMs` 1068.2 ms, inside a `dtMaxMs` of 1097.2 — a full second spent INSIDE the loop body on one frame, where the baseline row's worst body was 185.9 ms. It is almost certainly a cell build or a texture upload landing on the main thread as the camera crossed into new ground, and the instrument cannot say which: it keeps per-segment MEANS and only a whole-body maximum. Per-segment maxima are the next cheap thing the collector owes.

openQuestions: Which segment owns the 1068 ms body? The collector needs per-segment maxima to answer, and this is the second capture in which the worst frame is the interesting one.

`spans` is empty again, over a run that DID stream (the camera moved and cells changed level) — so the between-frame recorder still catches nothing on this path, and the 1-second body suggests why: the work is landing inside `engine.frame`, not between frames.
Water at 2.66 MB is 7.3 % of the read for a flat surface. What does the same shoreline cost as a heightfield the shader evaluates?
